recommended_next_phase: Phase 149O.20L.7B.1 -- Dell Boundary-P Proposition Materialization (Amendment). A narrow planning-only phase that must bind the pinned source commit SHA for Action 6, the exact immutable forward/read-back/rollback/rollback-verification command text for all nine actions, the exact literal launch-wrapper script content and environment contract for Action 8, and an explicit scope clarification that /opt/pcae/projects/<repo-slug>/repo is a future per-repository path template rather than standing repository-creation authority -- preserving the Dell target, Model-1 principal architecture, filesystem topology, nine-action structure, authority boundaries, exclusions, and product model unchanged. Must not provision. Must not hold a new election itself -- that follows in a subsequent 149O.20L.7B-style election phase.
summary: Phase 149O.20L.7B -- Dell Class-B Boundary-P Authorization Record Capture. AUTHORIZATION-RECORD-CAPTURE-ONLY phase. Reconstructed Phase 149O.20L.7A in full (its section 26 literal target values, section 27 nine-action plan, section 34 draft Boundary-P proposition) without paraphrasing before authorization. Live-reconfirmed Dell identity via a fresh, minimal, read-only SSH session (machine-id 54ff22ce400b475aa0d55cb68f4a3334, hostname atila-Latitude-E5470, Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, amd64) -- exact match to L.7A's own findings, so the election proceeded against the same host. Re-checked for material planning drift (no pcae principal/group/paths yet exist on the Dell; HBDC-001 v1.0/HMIC-001 v1.3/HMRC-001 v1.1 contract versions unchanged; codex sudo posture unchanged) -- none found, so the unmodified L.7A section 34 proposition was presented, not a paraphrase or a silently updated one. Presented the complete Dell-specific Boundary-P proposition to the human governance authority: target host/machine-id, pcae/pcae deployment principal (nologin, no SSH surface), existing codex sudo admin channel, every literal path from section 26, Model-A source binding, the three governing contract versions, the full nine-action graph with per-action privilege/read-back/rollback summarized, the explicit verifier-locality disclosure (the production Class-B verifier cannot evaluate the Dell from the Mac; no live Dell verifier result was fabricated by L.7A), the complete exclusion list, the per-repository product-model preservation statement, and the migration-scoping statement that authorization is Dell-specific and does not transfer to a future replacement host. Restated the authority wall (phase invocation is not itself an election; proposal is not approval; approval is not provisioning) immediately before requesting the election, with three options -- APPROVE, DECLINE, AMEND -- offered with no default and no inferred selection. The human governance authority elected AMEND, not APPROVE: preserve the Dell target, Model-1 principal architecture, filesystem topology, nine-action structure, authority boundaries, exclusions, and product model exactly as presented, but first materialize four remaining authority-bearing details before a new election -- (1) bind the exact PCAE source commit SHA to be cloned and installed; (2) bind the exact forward/read-back/rollback/rollback-verification commands for all nine actions by immutable proposition content or digest/reference; (3) bind the exact launch-wrapper content and environment contract; (4) clarify that /opt/pcae/projects/<repo-slug>/repo is a future per-repository path template, not authority to create arbitrary repositories during initial Dell provisioning -- explicitly stating no Dell mutation is authorized by the AMEND election itself. Ran the canonical pcae decision-session workflow (create, evidence with contract/document/commit/historical-CHGR-non-reuse citations, select with option-id amend against a closed approve/decline/amend options-presented set, preview with an independently reproduced preview_digest, confirm with the human's own separately requested closing first-person statement) through session CDS-cf123bbf-a5d7-4f0f-ac22-0baa257990af reaching Confirmed, then readiness constructing and persisting pending package prp-03cfe21aca284d009e71a2581c984dc0. pcae governance-record publish was deliberately not run, a disclosed judgment call: this phase's own governing instruction's AMEND semantics direct return to a narrow planning-amendment phase before a new election and do not include the DECLINE path's conditional publish-if-appropriate clause; a published CHGR is this repository's durable authority-record artifact for a concluded election, and AMEND is explicitly not a concluded election, so no chgr-*.json was created -- the Confirmed decision session and its persisted pending readiness package already provide a complete, preview-digest-bound, independently inspectable record of exactly what was presented and exactly what the human elected, without manufacturing a CHGR-shaped artifact for a non-terminal outcome. Confirmed via directory listing that .pcae/publication-execution/records/ still contains exactly the same four pre-existing files (the historical Mac CHGR chgr-d4343fa51b9743f3abaeb87a881a78b1 and its three sibling chgrconf-/chgrprov-/chgrintg- artifacts) as before this phase -- no new CHGR published, historical Mac CHGR neither modified nor reused, and the two artifacts (Mac CHGR vs. this phase's Dell-naming decision session) are unambiguously distinguishable by host identity. Assessed the four requested amendments as material, not cosmetic (each closes a genuine gap between L.7A's own descriptive prose and content that must be bound and immutable before an election can authorize 'the exact Dell proposition as presented'), and accordingly recommends the narrowest possible next phase rather than reinterpreting AMEND as a conditional approval. Boundary P remains NOT AUTHORIZED; Boundary C and Boundary A remain explicitly NOT AUTHORIZED; Class-B remains NOT PROVISIONED; HATP remains NOT READY; runtime unchanged (Observed/observe/unavailable). Every command run against the Dell this phase was read-only (identity/collision/sudo-posture checks only); the entire decision-session/readiness-package sequence executed locally against this repository's own .pcae/ state with no network call to the Dell. New, independently authored companion test module -- 27 tests, re-run three consecutive times, 27 passed each run, no flake -- asserting the historical Mac CHGR's continued isolation, the absence of any new Dell-naming CHGR, the persisted decision-session/readiness-package content (election=amend, session_state=Confirmed, subject naming the Dell by machine-id), the phase document's disclosures (verifier-locality, no-CHGR-published, materiality verdict, recommended next phase), and the absence of any literal Dell-mutating provisioning command in the phase document. Recommends exactly one next phase: 149O.20L.7B.1 -- Dell Boundary-P Proposition Materialization (Amendment), a narrow planning-only phase to bind the four requested amendment items -- pinned commit SHA, exact per-action command text, exact launch-wrapper content, and explicit per-repository-path-template scoping -- before a fresh 149O.20L.7B-style election phase is run. Not begun by this phase.
